documents.title: Types of Violations (Academic Integrity Policy, incl. AI-Generated Work)
documents.summary: IUP's academic integrity page defines violation types; its only AI content is that plagiarism covers AI-generated sources and that AI-generated work is unacceptable unless the instructor or administrator authorizes it.
documents.stance_why: The document says AI-generated work "is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator", a ban by default with permission possible, which is restrict rather than delegates.

units.why: The plagiarism definition says it "applies to any type of source, whether published or unpublished, human or AI-generated", so passing off AI output as one's own is a listed integrity violation; this is misconduct classification (P36) rather than a ban (P19) because the passage defines a violation category.
units.anchor: whether published or unpublished, human or AI-generated
units.policy: Plagiarism, an academic integrity violation, applies to AI-generated sources as well as human ones.

units.why: The policy requires that any work containing "the words, ideas, data, or creative works of another must include complete, accurate, and specific references"; with AI named as a source, this is a citation duty (P24), chosen over P25 because it does not name tool, prompt or date.
units.anchor: must include complete, accurate, and specific references
units.frag_start: Any assignment submitted by a student

units.why: "AI-generated work ... is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator" sets a default ban absent explicit permission, i.e. the fallback rule (P06); P04 is coded separately for who authorizes.
units.anchor: is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator
units.policy: AI-generated work is not acceptable unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator.

units.why: The same sentence makes the instructor or administrator the authority who may "authorize" AI-generated work, so permission is decided per instructor rather than by one university rule (P04).
units.anchor: unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator
units.policy: Whether AI-generated work is acceptable depends on specific authorization by the instructor/administrator.

units.why: The policy gives its reason: AI-generated work "is not reflective of a student’s own understanding and effort", a rationale that submitted work must reflect the student's own understanding, so P29 fits better than P41 (no claim about practice building skill).
units.anchor: not reflective of a student’s own understanding and effort

units.why: The page lists AI-Generated Work among IUP's "10 types of violations" of academic integrity, treating unauthorized AI use as misconduct handled under the integrity policy (P36).
units.anchor: IUP’s Academic Integrity policy outlines 10 types of violations.
units.policy: Unauthorized AI-generated work is one of the types of academic integrity violations under IUP's Academic Integrity policy.

notes: Thin source: one AI sentence plus the plagiarism clause.
